title: Nordet: follow-up on an overdue invoice
goal: Understand how a planned local portal turns an invented overdue invoice into an approved, simulated reminder, and why each safeguard is needed.

includes: The planned journey from invoice and rules to a simulated send
The safeguards listed in the Nordet scope document
excludes: Any running Nordet code: none exists yet, so this board describes intentions, not verified behavior
Real sends, real customer data, login, scheduling, LLM features, and deployment

groups.label: Portal screens
groups.description: What the user sees and acts on.

groups.label: Follow-up logic
groups.description: Decisions the app makes from the inputs.

groups.label: Local storage
groups.description: Data that must survive a restart.

components.label: Invoice and rules
components.summary: The invented CAD 100 overdue invoice and the follow-up rules that the user enters.
components.explanation: Everything starts here. The invoice is **invented**, and the rules come from the user, not from built-in delays.
inputs: Invoice details typed or loaded by the user
Follow-up rules typed by the user
outputs: Invoice and rules for the rule check

components.label: Fictional clock
components.summary: A date the user sets by hand, so the same scenario gives the same result every time.
inputs: A date chosen by the user

components.label: Rule check
components.summary: Compares the invoice with the rules and the fictional date, and proposes a follow-up action when a rule matches.
components.explanation: The rule check only *proposes*. It does not send anything.
outputs: A proposed action, or no action

components.label: Preview
components.summary: Shows the exact recipient and the exact message before anything can happen.
components.explanation: The user must see what would be sent, word for word. Approval of a vague summary would not protect anyone.
outputs: Exact recipient and message shown to the user

components.label: Approval
components.summary: The user approves or rejects one specific version of the proposed action.
components.explanation: Approval belongs to **one version** of the action. If the user edits the recipient or message, the old approval no longer counts.

components.label: Simulated send
components.summary: Pretends to send an approved action and shows the result. Nothing leaves the computer.
components.explanation:
The send must be blocked when the action is:

- not approved
- rejected
- already sent

components.label: Saved record
components.summary: Local SQLite storage that keeps decisions and send results across an app restart.
components.explanation: The safeguards only work if the app still remembers them after a restart. Otherwise a restart could allow a second send.

relationships.label: approved action version
relationships.explanation: Only an approval of the current version can start a simulated send.

items.text: What information must be saved to recognize the same action after a restart?
No SQLite driver is chosen yet.
The format of the rules that the user enters is not specified.
An action gets a new version whenever its recipient or message changes.

scenarios.title: Approve and simulate
scenarios.summary: The normal path from an overdue invoice to a simulated reminder.

steps.caption: The user enters the invented invoice and a rule, and sets the fictional clock past the due date.
The rule check finds that the rule matches and proposes a reminder.
The preview shows the exact recipient and message.
The user approves this version, and the decision is saved.
The simulated send runs and its result is saved.
The preview shows the proposed reminder.
The user rejects it. The rejection is saved.
No simulated send is allowed for a rejected action.
The user edits the message. This makes a new version of the action.
The earlier approval was for the old version, so the send is blocked until the user approves the new one.
An approved reminder was already simulated as sent, and the result was saved.
The app restarts. The saved record still holds the earlier send.
The user tries the same send again. The send checks the saved record and refuses.
